page: Amazon Web Services g5g.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64-based AWS Graviton2 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated physical cores across 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 32.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA T4G GPU based on the Turing architecture with 16 GB of VRAM. The instance has no bundled local storage and includes a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent average throughput in multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core at 8557.0 points. Software compilation with Clang and ray tracing tests also achieve median performance levels. Conversely, single-core processing shows bottlenecks, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 948.0, weak gzip compression, and poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory benchmark scores and PassMark CPU encryption tests also rank in the lower quartile. In language model inference, prompt processing throughput is low on small and medium models, while text generation on a 7B model reaches an average 10.67 tokens per second.

With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and ARM-native processing, the g5g.4xlarge offers resource density tailored for graphics and inference workloads built for ARM64 architectures. The lack of local NVMe storage requires external network-attached volumes for persistent data. This instance is best aligned with Android cloud streaming, graphics rendering, image processing, video transcoding, and entry-level machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services g5g.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance utilizing the Nitro hypervisor, powered by a 16-core ARM64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs without multithreading, 32.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core, and a dedicated NVIDIA T4G GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. It includes 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and contains no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, multi-core metrics, static web serving, and database operations exhibit average throughput, while single-core performance and cryptographic operations score in lower tiers. Inference benchmarks show moderate text generation speeds on 7B models alongside constrained prompt processing throughput. The instance delivers a balanced hardware profile for cost-conscious, ARM64-optimized environments. Suitable workloads include Android cloud gaming, image processing, ray tracing, video encoding, and entry-level GPU inference pipelines that do not require local ephemeral NVMe storage.
